newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Dampened by spate of late offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Dampened by spate of late offers.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market eased on Friday after high stocks, arbitrage cargoes and lower swaps quotes dampened prices, traders said on Friday.
Late Friday, a 20,000 tonne 180-cst cargo for loading in mid April was traded at $102.50 per tonne.
Earlier in the day, bids/offers for 180-cst was quoted ranging between $101-$105.50 per tonne for cargoes loading in April, compared to Thursday's quotes at $103-$105 per tonne.
But prices eased later in the day when more offers emerged, ranging between $102.50/$103 per year.
"Supplies are adequate," one trader said. "The chinese are expected to buy less in April as their import tariffs will be adjusted upwards," he said.
China fuel oil import tariffs will be increased to 6.0 percent from the previous 3.0 percent starting April 1.

Some traders attribute the price fall to high stock figures. They said stocks levels in Singapore are high despite the 932,000-barrels draw to 11.76 million barrels for the week ending March 19 as in the previous week there was a 2.097 million barrel build.
Arbitrage cargoes arriving from the west were also expected to keep prices under pressure.
In the fuel oil swaps market, prices also came off as more offers than bids emerged in the market.
The April swaps were last quoted at $99.50/$100.50, compared with Thursday's $103.00/$104.00.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
